author: reek
body: A height field is marched rather than rasterised because the model is a FUNCTION of x and z, not a mesh. The ocean renderer builds a grid and fills triangles because it needs the surface at controlled positions; here the surface can be asked about anywhere, and marching gives an exact silhouette along every ridge line instead of one quantised to a grid.

author: reek
body: Traced at half resolution and written as 2x2 blocks, for the reason `CloudRender` gives.

author: reek
body: Cleared to magenta first so a capture that lands mid-draw is obvious rather than plausible. See the note in `CloudRender`; it was written after a partial frame was mistaken for a finished one.

author: reek
body: A linear march with a GROWING step. Uniform steps small enough to catch a ridge close to the camera are far more than are needed a kilometre out, where one step already covers less than a pixel; growing the step spends the samples where the silhouette actually is. It is the same reasoning as the lengthening stride in the cloud model's light march.

author: reek
body: The march finds the first step whose end is under the terrain, which brackets the surface between two samples but locates it only to within a step. Bisecting that bracket is what makes the silhouette clean: without it the ridge lines are visibly quantised into the step size, and no affordable step count hides that.

author: reek
body: **This cap is NOT what fixed the terracing, and it was blamed for it.** The first render came out in stair-step contours, the bracket argument above was the obvious explanation, the cap was added, and the terraces did not move at all. The cause was in the material blend, not here; see the note on `terrain-splat-scale` in `TerrainModel`, and the pair of experiments that cornered it. Rendering with a constant albedo is what cleared this file: the surface came out smooth, so the march and the normals were never the problem.

author: reek
body: The cap stays, because the reasoning for it is sound on its own terms and the bracket really can hold two crossings. The note stays because the same reasoning was sound for an artifact it was innocent of, and a mechanism that plausibly explains the wrong thing is more expensive than no explanation at all -- it stops the search.

author: reek
body: `-screenshot` captures at `-screenshot-delay` and ends the run there, so the guest must still be alive with a finished frame when the timer fires. Too short and the capture lands mid-draw; too long and no file is written at all. The hold is deliberately generous so the delay need not be exact.
